correctness.rationale: For b>1 and -1<N,D<1, each alpha_j=sqrt((1+Nq^j)/(1+Dq^j)) is strictly positive and tends geometrically to 1. Beta_k=product_{j<k}alpha_j converges to P>0, so diagonal X e_j=beta_j e_j is bounded/invertible with W X=X S. If N>D the decreasing weights yield ||W^k||=beta_k, whence every invertible intertwiner has condition at least beta_k and then P; if N<D the increasing contractive weights have m(W^k)=beta_k and the S-isometry similarity gives condition at least 1/beta_k, then 1/P. In both cases the diagonal X attains, including N=D. Euler–Maclaurin applied to f(x)=log[(1+Ne^-x)/(1+De^-x)] with integrable derivatives gives log P=(Li2(-D)-Li2(-N))/(2h)+f(0)/4+O(h), h=log b, and both terms have common sign. With N=d+tau h, D=d, uniform Taylor expansion gives log P ->(tau/2)log(1+d)/d, with d=0 continuously 1. Independent finite product computations confirmed order-of-magnitude for three parameter pairs at b=1.1 and 1.01. The proof is exact operator-power and Riemann-sum analysis, not numerical sampling.
